rows.abstract: REPEALS Article 3 of Presidential Decree No. 1620, entitled "An Act Granting to the International Rice Research Institute(IRRI) the Status, Privileges and Immunicites of an International Organization". Seeks to rectify the loopholes of the existinglaw which curtails the rights of its hapless Filipino workers.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on REVISION OF LAWS since 1999-07-27

rows.title_full: AN ACT PROVIDING FOR THE ESTABLISHMENT OF ELECTRONIC LIBRARY IN EACH AND EVERY PUBLIC SCHOOL IN THE PHILIPPINES IN ORDER TO ASSIST PUBLIC ELEMENTARY AND SECONDARY SCHOOL TEACHERS IN EDUCATING THEIR RESPECTIVE STUDENT AND APPROPRIATING FUNDS THEREFOR
rows.abstract: "Electronic Library Act of 1999." Intends to modernize the educational materials and tools in the dissemination of knowledge and information to strengthen and broaden scientific and technical knowledge, and promote vocational efficiency among students. Provides for the guidelines al funds as to administration, school preference, priority materials and requirements and procedures for the purchase of supplies and equipment.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on BASIC EDUCATION since 1999-07-27

rows.title_full: AN ACT PROVIDING FOR THE INCREASE IN MEDICAL CARE BENEFITS UNDER PRESIDENTIAL DECREE NO. 1519 OTHERWISE KNOWN AS THE `REVISED PHILIPPINE MEDICAL CARE ACT' TO COVER NO LESS THAN SEVENTY-FIVE PERCENT (75%) OF MEDICAL EXPENSES INCURRED BY MEDICARE MEMBERS
rows.abstract: Aims to alleviate the difficulty of ordinary workers in meeting hospitalization and other medical expenses by providing more realistic rates of medical care benefits to medicare members. Tasks the Philippine Medical Care Commission to REVISE the present rates of medical care benefits to SEVENTY-FIVE PERCENT (75%) to conform to the increase provided in this Act. Increases therefore the rate of contribution of its members to meet the needed additional funds.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on HEALTH since 1999-07-27

rows.title_full: AN ACT REQUIRING ALL HIGH SCHOOL STUDENTS TO PLANT FIVE TREES A YEAR AS A PRE-CONDITION FOR THEIR GRADUATION FROM HIGH SCHOOL
rows.abstract: Sees an urgent need to replenish our timber lands so that the future generation will still have some forest resources to enjoy by inculcating in the student's young minds ecological consciousness and the need to preserve nature as a vital factor inour development efforts.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on BASIC EDUCATION since 1999-07-27

rows.title_full: AN ACT ESTABLISHING A SENIOR CITIZEN LODGING HOUSE IN ALL CAPITAL TOWNS AND MAJOR CITIES IN THE COUNTRY AND APPROPRIATING FUNDS THEREFOR
rows.abstract: Establishes a lodging house with adequate facilites and amenities designed to cater to the needs and welfare of senior citizens while they are traveling within the country and thus promote local tourism. Exempts such Houses from the payment of custom duties, taxes and tariff on the importation of equipment and supplies used by and donated thereto.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on POPULATION AND FAMILY RELATIONS since 1999-07-27

rows.author: C088
rows.title_full: AN ACT TO PRESCRIBE THE ESTABLISHMENT OF PILOT TRIBAL COMMUNITIES AND/OR HOUSING PROJECTS IN EACH AND EVERY REGION IN THE PHILIPPINES, INCLUDING METRO MANILA, WHICH SHALL SERVE AS MODEL HUMAN SETTLEMENTS THAT WILL ADHERE, TO THE EXTENT PRACTICABLE,TO THE CULTURE AND TRADITIONS OF THE NATIONAL TRIBAL COMMUNITIES, WHILE PROVIDING  THE BASIC CONVENIENCES OF MODERN LIVING, APPROPRIATING FUNDS THEREFOR AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES 1
rows.abstract: The bill prescribes the establishment of pilot tribal communities and/or housing projects in each and every region in the Philippines. Declares that the policy of the State is to establish, maintain and ensure adequate shelter, education, health, employment, welfare and other social services to national tribal communities.

rows.title_full: AN ACT AMENDING SECTION 9 OF REPUBLIC ACT NO. 7432 OTHERWISE KNOWN AS `AN ACT TO MAXIMIZE THE CONTRIBUTION OF SENIOR CITIZENS TO NATION-BUILDING , GRANT BENEFITS AND SPECIAL PRIVILEGES AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES,' BY INCREASING THE PENALTIES FOR THE VIOLATION OF ANY PROVISIONS THEREOF
rows.abstract: Violation of any provision of this Act for which no penalty is specifically provided under any other law, shall be punished by imprisonment OF UP TO SIX (6) MONTHS or a fine FROM FIVE THOUSAND PESOS (P5,000.00) TO TEN THOUSAND PESOS (P10,000.00) orboth.  IN CASES INVOLVING PRIVATE ESTABLISHMENTS WHICH REFUSE TO GRANT BENEFITS TO SENIOR CITIZENS, SUBSEQUENT OFFENSES WILL RESULT IN THE REVOCATION OF THEIR FRANCHISE OR BUSINESS PERMITS BY AUTHORIZED GOVERNMENT AGENCIES.

rows.title_full: AN ACT AMENDING SECTION 90, PERTAINING TO THE PRACTICE OF PROFESSION, OF REPUBLIC ACT NO. 7160, OTHERWISE KNOWN AS THE LOCAL GOVERNMENT CODE OF 1991
rows.abstract: Many of these elective local government officials are compelled to give-up their lucrative practice of profession to their personal detriment. On the other hand, it is still possible to allow them a limited practice of their profession that will notbe detrimental to their functions as local government official. This bill seeks to carve out that middle ground by distinguishing among the different local government officials and defining to what extent they may practice their profession.
